export_controls.description: $39B manufacturing subsidies + $13B R&D. Recipients barred from expanding chip fabs in China for 10 years. 25% investment tax credit for US fab construction.
First sweeping controls blocking A100-class+ chips to China. Introduced TPP and performance-density thresholds. Also restricted semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
Japan restricted 23 types of advanced chip manufacturing equipment (lithography, etching, deposition). Expanded by 21 items in Apr 2024. China stockpiled $5B in equipment pre-deadline.

China imposed export licenses on gallium and germanium. Escalated to graphite (Oct 2023), antimony (Aug 2024), tungsten (Feb 2025), rare earths (Apr 2025). Full US halt Dec 2024. Partially suspended Nov 2025 under trade truce.
Blocked ASML from selling advanced DUV immersion lithography to China. Expanded Sep 2024 to require licenses for 1970i/1980i DUV machines. ASML China revenue projected to drop from 29% to ~20%.
Closed loopholes — blocked A800/H800 China workaround variants. Added performance-density thresholds capturing RTX 4090 gaming GPU. Expanded Entity List.
NVIDIA released downgraded H20 and L20 chips designed to comply with US thresholds for the China market. Reduced memory bandwidth and compute performance vs H100.

export_controls.target: EU + any entity selling AI in EU
export_controls.description: World's first comprehensive AI law. Risk-based framework: prohibited/high/limited/minimal risk tiers. Penalties up to EUR 35M or 7% global turnover. Phase 1 (prohibited practices) Feb 2025, Phase 2 (GPAI) Aug 2025, Phase 3 (high-risk) Aug 2026.

export_controls.regulation: Biden Entity List + HBM Controls + FDPR Expansion
export_controls.description: Added 140 entities to Entity List (fabs, tool makers, Huawei suppliers). First country-wide HBM export controls to China. Expanded Foreign Direct Product Rule scope. Restricted advanced AI chip packaging tech.

3-tier global system: Tier 1 (18 allies) unrestricted; Tier 2 (~150 countries) quantity caps ~50K GPUs/entity; Tier 3 (~25 countries incl. China) prohibited. Also controlled AI model weights. Rescinded by Trump admin May 2025 before compliance date.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 1 — Prohibited Practices
export_controls.description: Ban on social scoring, emotion recognition in workplaces/schools, untargeted facial scraping, predictive crime assessment. First enforcement phase of EU AI Act.
Eliminated Biden's 3-tier country system and quantity caps 2 days before compliance date. Replaced with bilateral deal-based approach. Pre-existing China entity-level controls remain.
Declared using/selling/servicing Huawei Ascend 910B/C/D chips anywhere violates US export controls under Foreign Direct Product Rule. Extraterritorial worldwide scope.
Draft BIS rule requiring export licenses for AI GPU shipments to Malaysia/Thailand — evidence of transshipment to China. Enhanced documentation and end-use verification.
Export license for NVIDIA/AMD to sell H20-class chips to China with 15% of China sales revenue paid to US government. First-ever revenue-sharing arrangement tied to export licenses.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 2 — GPAI Obligations
export_controls.description: General-Purpose AI model obligations take effect. AI Office becomes operational. Compute reporting requirements for GPAI providers. Governance infrastructure established.
Commerce authorized 70,000 NVIDIA GB300 chips to HUMAIN (Saudi) and G42 (UAE). Ended regulatory standoff blocking billions in data center investments. Part of US-Gulf AI partnership.
China suspended export controls on gallium, germanium, antimony, graphite, and rare earths for 1 year under trade truce. General licenses issued for US end users. Can be reimposed at any time.

export_controls.regulation: Trump H200 to China (25% Revenue Share)
export_controls.description: Authorized NVIDIA H200 sales to vetted Chinese customers with 25% revenue share to US government (up from 15% for H20). Near-cutting-edge chips to China under commercial terms. Bipartisan criticism.
First SE Asian comprehensive AI law. Phased implementation starting Mar 2026 over 4 years. Establishes AI governance framework for Vietnamese market.

Codified shift from 'presumption of denial' to 'case-by-case review' for H200/MI325X-class exports to China. Requires: sufficient US domestic supply, no foundry capacity diversion, third-party testing, and recipient security procedures.

25% tariff on imported advanced AI semiconductors, SME, and derivative products. Broad exemptions for US data center imports, R&D, startups, consumer use, and public sector. Impact review due Jul 2026.

Congressional oversight of AI chip exports like arms sales. Creates 'Trusted US Person' framework for ally deployments. Would temporarily revoke existing China licenses pending national security strategy review. Passed committee markup Jan 2026.

ISM 2.0 expanded beyond fab subsidies to semiconductor equipment, materials, and IP. 10 approved fab projects; $38B domestic market targeting $100B by 2030. Government subsidizes AI compute at Rs 65/GPU-hr vs global $2-3/hr.

export_controls.regulation: EU AI Act Phase 3 — High-Risk AI Systems
export_controls.description: Full compliance for high-risk standalone AI systems: biometrics, critical infrastructure, employment, law enforcement, education, migration. Conformity assessments and CE marking required.

basis_legend.measured: Read from a live external source this run.
basis_legend.reference: Curated from published documents; refreshed manually.
basis_legend.modeled: Estimate. No public source exists for these numbers.
basis_legend.mixed: Contains both measured and estimated fields — see detail.

providers.detail: Live provider APIs and published price lists. Every price carries a source and last_verified; nothing is published without one.

matrix.detail: Recomputed from providers + specs on each run.

spot.detail: Aggregated from provider prices. bid/ask are a modelled spread around the live average, not a traded quote.

historical.detail: Monthly min/average/max per GPU, aggregated from the daily per-provider price record over the provider set tracked today, so a provider joining or leaving cannot read as a price move. Replaces a series that spliced a hand-seeded era onto live figures: it showed H100 doubling in a month and drove a false 202% year-on-year rise into the volatility panel, which then labelled six GPUs 'tightening' while prices were flat or falling. It starts at 2026-05 because live scraping replaced hardcoded seed prices on 2026-04-30 and nothing before that is comparable -- short and true rather than long and spliced.

summary.detail: Recomputed from matrix, providers and indicators.

tco.detail: Cloud rates track live provider averages; includes commitment break-even (formerly a separate reservations dataset). Power/colo/staff inputs are overridable in the Scenario Builder.

inference.detail: OpenRouter. Token and request volumes are the published daily rankings figures; per-provider prices, quantization, context and uptime come from /api/v1/models/{slug}/endpoints. The roster was previously copied by hand and went stale between edits; it is now whatever the rankings say that day. Trend history is accumulated here one observation per run, so it starts short and lengthens.

news.detail: Google News RSS. Dates are as published.

sentiment.detail: Reddit, HuggingFace and GitHub APIs. Composite scores are our own weighting.

indicators.detail: Stock prices are live (Yahoo Finance). Market size and AI capex are derived from reported company revenue and guidance. Shipment counts are estimates.

sustainability.detail: Per-GPU energy, carbon and water computed from specs.tdp_watts each run, using the five constants in sustainability.assumptions (sustained load 82% of TDP, US grid 0.40 kg CO2e/kWh, Nordic 0.045, water 1.8 L/kWh, embodied 200 kg/kW). Previously a hand-written table that covered 9 of 17 GPUs and had drifted from specs -- GB200 carried the 2700W superchip TDP against a per-GPU price, overstating its power and carbon 2.25x. Embodied carbon is an order-of-magnitude estimate; the rest is arithmetic. Provider PUE and grid figures alongside this are from published sustainability reports.

supplychain.detail: Export-control timeline is public record; vendor risk scores are editorial. Regional unit-count inventories have been removed.

regional.detail: Same Azure VM SKU priced across regions via the Retail Prices API. Replaces modelled regional market share.

modelfit.detail: Open-weights models from the current demand leaderboard, sized against live GPU prices. Parameter counts are the exact totals from each model's HuggingFace safetensors index; layers, KV heads and head dim come from its config.json. VRAM = weights + KV cache + 20% overhead for activations and fragmentation -- that 20% is the only assumption. MoE models hold every expert in VRAM, so weights use total parameters while the active count is reported separately. Break-even throughput solves for the output tokens/sec a rig must sustain to beat the cheapest API route for the same model, so no throughput figure is invented.

volatility.detail: Realized volatility, drawdown and trend per GPU, computed from the daily market average across the providers tracked today. Previously computed from the monthly series, which after being rebuilt on one comparable basis holds four points -- three returns. Annualized volatility is only reported where at least 20 daily returns stand behind it, and the observation count is published with every figure.

changelog.detail: Price movements between consecutive refreshes. Moves over 100% are flagged for review rather than published as signal.

prediction_markets.detail: Live order books: Kalshi trade API and Polymarket Gamma API. Implied prices are read off the quoted ladder/brackets (median of the market-implied distribution) -- no model of ours. Both venues settle against the Ornn GPU compute index, which is not the same basket as our provider list-price average, so the two series are related but not directly comparable.

price_history.detail: Each provider's published price per GPU, per day. Backfilled from the git history of data.json -- every commit is an exact record of what was published that day -- and appended once per run thereafter. The change feed was not used: it only logs moves of 3% or more, so a series rebuilt from it drifts. Windows containing one of this pipeline's own scraper corrections are flagged, because those moves are not the market.

ai_analysis.detail: Language-model commentary over the snapshot of this data. Not a forecast. Each block carries its generation date; blocks older than 7 days are flagged on the page.

term_structure.detail: On-demand and committed rates for the top-tier GPUs, read from each provider's published price list (AWS Savings Plans and Reserved Instances, Azure reservations, GCP committed use, Lambda 1-Click Cluster reservations, Together reserved clusters, DigitalOcean 12-month reserved). Discounts compare a commitment with the SAME provider's on-demand rate; multi-node cluster reservations are listed but kept out of the discount medians. status.status: The one-year Busan truce of Oct 2025 was formally extended on Nov 9, 2026 to January 10, 2027: tariff reductions kept, China suspends critical-mineral export controls and its 24% tariff on US goods for two months.
Suspension extended again to January 10, 2027 (was due to lapse Nov 2026), in line with the extended US-China trade truce.

US allows H200 under case-by-case licenses with a 25% cut, but Beijing still withholds approval for large-scale imports: ~600,000 H200s sit in Hong Kong, and several major Chinese internet firms have each received only ~10,000.

NVIDIA took a $0.4B H200 excess-inventory charge in H1 FY27; licensed H200 shipments were <1% of Data Center revenue, must pass US inspection and carry a 25% US import tariff, and NVIDIA assumes no China data-center compute revenue in guidance.

Rescinded by BIS on May 13, 2025 with a promise of a replacement rule; as of June 2026 no replacement had been issued, and GAO ruled (May 12, 2026) that the non-enforcement announcement was itself a 'rule' under the Congressional Review Act.
House Foreign Affairs Committee advanced the Chip Security Act (anti-smuggling / location-verification for exported AI chips) on March 26, 2026; full House passage not verified.
April 2025 license requirement on H20 led to a $4.5B charge; licenses granted August 2025 yielded only ~$60M of H20 revenue, with US officials expecting 15%+ of licensed revenue (never codified).

Proclamation signed Jan 14, 2026 imposes an immediate 25% tariff on a narrow set of advanced computing chips (e.g., H200, MI325X), with exemptions for chips used in US data centers, R&D and other domestic uses; broader phase depends on negotiations.

Trump announced on Dec 8, 2025 that H200 exports to approved Chinese customers would be allowed with a 25% fee; BIS moved H200/MI325X license reviews to case-by-case (rule issued Jan 13, effective Jan 15, 2026) subject to security requirements.

takeaways: Published commitments on H100 save a median 33% for 1 year and 56% for 3 years against the same provider's on-demand rate; they pay off above 67% and 44% utilisation.

The cheapest published 3-year H100 rate ($2.97, Amazon Web Services) sits above the cheapest dedicated-cloud on-demand price ($1.99, Together AI): where you buy moves the price as much as how long you commit.
Short-term blocks are priced close to on-demand: AWS Capacity Blocks run 0% (B200) to 13% (H100-SXM) below us-east-1 on-demand, against 37-62% for a 1-3 year Savings Plan.
Region matters: Azure MI300X on-demand runs $6.00 (eastus2) to $12.00 (brazilsouth), 2.0x apart, and committed rates scale with it.

contracts.method: Curated, citation-backed list of large multi-year compute/capacity contracts. Every number was read from the cited url (or a second url named in the note) on 2026-11-12. confidence: 'disclosed' = stated by a party (press release, blog or SEC filing); 'reported' = not disclosed by the companies, taken from reputable press as noted. Most values are 'up to' ceilings subject to delivery, availability and termination conditions, not guaranteed payments. term_years is the stated term where there is one; for CoreWeave rows it is the span from signing to the stated end date, noted per row. Implied $/GPU-hr is computed only when value, term and GPU count for the same contract are all disclosed or reported: value / (gpus x 8760 x years), or monthly fee x 12 / (gpus x 8760). It assumes every GPU is billed for the whole term (deliveries are often phased, which would raise the true rate) and includes everything the contract bundles (networking, storage, CPUs, power, data center, services), so it is an upper bound on pure GPU cost. Rows with an implied price have confidence 'estimate'; their inputs are disclosed figures. GPU counts are never inferred from MW. Colocation leases (Fluidstack rows) are power/space, not compute, and must not be compared with GPU-hour prices. Rows for the same buyer and seller can overlap (CoreWeave-OpenAI tranches sum to the ~$22.4B CoreWeave reported; the Nscale Narvik row may be inside the Nscale $43.8B aggregate).
